comparison: Perfect agreement on HDX-MS findings showing Ric-8A-induced destabilization of G-protein structure. Both evaluations find the data well-supported with high quality evidence. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls and convergent evidence from DEER spectroscopy, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the central hypothesis about stabilizing poorly ordered nucleotide-free G protein.

Strong agreement on comparative HDX-MS data across GDP, Ric-8A-bound, and GTP states. OpenEval explicitly validates the data quality and interpretation, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the overall high-quality technical work. Peer review includes C122 not mentioned in OpenEval result.

Perfect agreement on identification of C-terminal Ric-8A region (454-470) as G-protein binding site. Both evaluations find the HDX protection data compelling and the inference reasonable. Peer reviewers explicitly quote and support this finding.

Strong agreement on mutagenesis validation of the C-terminal binding site. Both evaluations praise the experimental rigor, statistical analysis, and biochemical validation. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance of specific mutants, while peer reviewers note the biophysical analysis is augmented by biochemical validation. Peer review includes C142-C143 (DSF data) which OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Agreement on C-terminal helix and broad interaction surface, but peer reviewers suggest softening tone about C-terminus role in light of recent A2A receptor structures. OpenEval finds claims appropriately qualified with 'may', while peer reviewers request more nuanced interpretation regarding nucleotide exchange mechanism.

Agreement on domain interface interactions and switch region involvement. Both evaluations accept the convergence of HDX and EPR data. OpenEval addresses C9-C10, C96-C99, C177, C179 while peer review covers broader set including C178, C180-C188 (mechanistic interpretation of selectivity). Both note key differences from GPCR mechanisms.

Both address comparison between Ric-8A and GPCR mechanisms. OpenEval focuses on extensive interface and mechanistic synthesis (C148-C149, C176, C190-C193), while peer reviewers focus on similarities and differences in G-protein interaction (C148-C158, C165-C166, C176). Peer reviewers suggest softening tone and discussing NMR data from Ridge lab.

Overlapping coverage of dual GEF/chaperone mechanism. OpenEval R7 addresses extensive interface and mechanistic proposals (C190-C193), while peer R10 explicitly affirms the central hypothesis about chaperone function. Both find the mechanistic interpretation reasonable and appropriately cautious.

Partial overlap on distinguishing Ric-8A effects from nucleotide-free state characteristics. OpenEval addresses C165-C166, C175 with support from NMR comparisons, while peer review covers broader mechanistic comparison (C148-C158, C165-C166, C176) and suggests discussing Ridge lab NMR results.

Both address evidence that changes are due to Ric-8A rather than nucleotide-free state alone. OpenEval R8 focuses on C165-C166, C175 with NMR comparisons, while peer R9 addresses C50-C54, C172-C175 affirming the chaperone hypothesis and suggesting discussion of Ridge lab NMR data on partially unfolded states.

Agreement on dual GEF/chaperone mechanism and mechanistic inferences. OpenEval addresses C194-C197 finding the interpretation reasonable, while peer reviewers explicitly support the central hypothesis about stabilizing poorly ordered G protein. Both find the mechanistic interpretation appropriately cautious.

Strong overlap on experimental methodology and data quality. OpenEval addresses materials, methods, and technical aspects (C63-C76, C208), while peer reviewers affirm high technical quality and rigorous experimental design. Peer reviewers request moving supplemental figures to main text as they show primary data.

Divergent evaluations of Ric-8A computational model. OpenEval finds the Robetta predictions appropriately cited and reasonable (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers express uncertainty and ask for validation by CD or other biophysical measures (UNCERTAIN). Both acknowledge limitations of computational predictions without experimental structure.

Agreement on HDX findings for Ric-8A conformational changes upon G-protein binding. OpenEval finds data supported though interpretation of 'distributive conformational changes' somewhat speculative, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these observations as part of high-quality data identifying multiple interaction sites.

Both address DSF data showing no correlation between thermal stability and GEF activity. OpenEval finds this important for ruling out global destabilization (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers accept the biochemical validation as part of rigorous experimental design (SUPPORTED).

Agreement on HDX-MS technical quality and the distinction between fast and slow exchange dynamics. OpenEval addresses C77-C79 finding the characterization important, while peer reviewers affirm high technical quality and request primary HDX data be featured more prominently in main figures.

Agreement on protection patterns indicating Ric-8A shielding of specific regions. OpenEval addresses C87-C88, C94-C95 finding the inference reasonable with appropriate speculative language, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of multiple identified interaction sites without specific challenge.

Partial overlap on background claims about Ric-8A. OpenEval finds background claims C1-C2, C11-C37 appropriately cited (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers address C28-C29, C30, C35 suggesting Ric-8 be referred to as having GEF activity rather than being called a physiological GEF, indicating agreement with cautious language.

Disagreement on scope of claim about Ric-8A characterization. OpenEval finds background claim C12 appropriately cited (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers explicitly challenge it as too broad (UNSUPPORTED), stating it's only true for heterotrimeric G-proteins and needs qualification since cytosolic exchange factors for Ras are very well understood.

Both address background on G-proteins and prior work. OpenEval covers C38-C54 as appropriately cited background (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers address subset C50-C54, C172-C175 in context of affirming the chaperone hypothesis and suggesting discussion of Ridge lab NMR data.
OpenEval addresses HDX-MS methodological principles (C55-C59) as appropriately cited background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these methodological claims.

Partial overlap on GPCR mechanism background. OpenEval addresses C150-C164 as appropriately cited background for comparison (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers address subset C148-C158, C165-C166, C176 in context of comparing Ric-8A and GPCR mechanisms, suggesting softening tone about C-terminus role.

Agreement on use of prior NMR studies to support interpretation. OpenEval addresses C172-C174 as appropriate use of literature (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers address C50-C54, C172-C175 affirming the interpretation and suggesting discussion of Ridge lab NMR results on partially unfolded states.

Strong overlap on mechanistic explanation of Ric-8A selectivity for GDP-bound G-protein. OpenEval addresses C178-C189 as well-supported synthesis of structural knowledge (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers address C9, C96-C99, C177-C188 noting key differences from GPCRs including broad flexibility increases and switch region interactions.

Agreement on methodological rigor and documentation. OpenEval addresses detailed methods C198-C217 as well-documented with appropriate controls and replicates (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers affirm rigorous experimental design and high technical quality, requesting primary data be featured more prominently.
